items.claim: Predictable sequential IDs turn IDOR from a lucky find into enumeration: with no ownership check on the object reference, the id space can be walked with one low-privilege session.
items.disproof: Refuted when the server performs an ownership check on every object reference: an unauthorised request must return 403/404, not another user's object. Low entropy in the ID alone is not the finding.

sources.quote: Note when identifiers are sequential or predictable – if your ID is 64185742, then 64185741 probably exists.
Insecure direct object references (IDOR) are a type of access control vulnerability that arises when an application uses user-supplied input to access objects directly.

items.claim: The minimal IDOR proof keeps one authenticated low-privilege session fixed and changes only the object ID, so any difference in the response is attributable to the missing authorization check rather than to session state.
items.body: HackTricks reference: IDOR - proof of concept shape
items.disproof: Refuted when the two responses are indistinguishable, or when the second object belongs to the same principal: a different body alone proves nothing about cross-user access.

sources.quote: Use an authenticated low-privilege session and change only the ID keeping the same token/cookie.
